title: Hazel and the Autopsy
premise: True-crime podcaster Marguerite Yarrow arrives in the fog-bound town of Grayhollow to investigate the century-old disappearance of a witness to the founder's death — only for the town council's ceremonial exhumation of that founder, Aldous Vane, to reveal an empty coffin and a body buried in his place. As Marguerite digs into the autopsy records, they discover the 'dead' witness, Hazel Finch, may have survived by trading her silence, and that Grayhollow's founding families have been paying that price ever since. When Marguerite finally traces Hazel to a hospice on the coast, the dying woman gives them the confession that unravels the town's mythology — but exposing it means destroying the found family of descendants who sheltered Marguerite through the investigation. In the end, Marguerite broadcasts the truth anyway, choosing the case over belonging, and Hazel dies free with her name restored.
about_author: Ada Pemberton is the pen name of a former coroner's assistant turned novelist who spent a decade transcribing autopsy reports in small-town morgues. They write mysteries about the secrets towns bury and the people stubborn enough to dig them up.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case
chapters.summary: Marguerite Yarrow, POV. In their studio, Marguerite introduces the Grayhollow case: in 1924, witness Hazel Finch vanished after testifying about founder Aldous Vane's death, and no record of her exists beyond one signature. Marguerite's rule is never take a case they can't close. The beat is confident obsession — and the first crack in it, as their producer warns them this one feels different.

chapters.title: What the Coffin Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Arriving in Grayhollow during the centennial exhumation ceremony, Marguerite watches the council open Aldous Vane's monument — and find it empty except for the remains of a young woman wearing Hazel Finch's locket. The crowd's festive mood curdles. Emotional beat: vertigo; the case Marguerite came to narrate has just rewritten itself in front of everyone.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Town archives yield a death certificate for Hazel dated 1925 — signed by the same doctor whose descendant now runs the council. Every elder Marguerite interviews repeats the same rehearsed grief. But a retired gravedigger lets slip that Vane's plot was opened once before, quietly, in 1961. Beat: the town's unity begins to look like choreography.

chapters.title: The Yarrow Rule
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV, with interludes from producer Dev's voicemails. Marguerite befriends the Corliss siblings, young descendants of the founding families who run the diner and seem genuinely kind — the found family taking shape. Yet their warmth comes with gentle steering away from certain files. Beat: belonging offered at exactly the moment honesty would cost it.

chapters.title: Autopsy of a Lie
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. A leaked 1961 report shows the woman buried in Vane's coffin died of arsenic poisoning — administered over years, not days. Cross-referencing hospice ledgers, Marguerite finds a resident named 'H. Fenn' admitted decades ago under a false name, still alive. Beat: triumph curdling into dread, because someone clearly wanted this trail cold.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Hazel Fenn (Finch), POV, in flashbacks interwoven with Marguerite's present-day drive to the coast. We learn Hazel faked her death in 1924, was hunted, poisoned slowly by the families to guarantee silence, and survived by becoming exactly what they believed: dead. Beat: devastating cost of survival — she lived, but only as a ghost.

chapters.title: Kindness with Conditions
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Back in Grayhollow, Marguerite discovers the Corliss siblings knew about Hazel all along — their family's wealth depends on the settlement built on her silence. Their offer: drop the story, stay, become one of them. Marguerite, lonely and half-in-love with the town, wavers. Beat: temptation at its most human.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: Alternating Marguerite and Hazel POVs. Hazel is dying; the families learn Marguerite found her and move to have her declared incompetent and her records sealed. Dev warns Marguerite their sources are being burned one by one. Beat: rising panic — every hour of hesitation hands the town another shovel.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Autopsy
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Hazel, shared scene, POV alternating within it. At the hospice, Hazel dictates her full confession: she saw the founding families kill Vane, and the empty coffin was their insurance policy all along. She asks Marguerite to promise two things — tell the truth, and don't let them make you pay for it. Beat: quiet, luminous climax of trust.

chapters.title: Signed in Full
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Marguerite broadcasts the episode live from the courthouse steps, naming names, ending the Yarrow rule of guaranteed closure — some cases can only be closed by breaking your own heart. The Corlisses turn away; Hazel dies that night with her real name read aloud on air. Final beat: grief and integrity entwined; Marguerite walks out of Grayhollow alone, carrying a new family made of listeners who finally know the truth.
